import pandas as pd
from itables import show
from IPython.display import display, HTML

mvp_prob_df = pd.read_csv("mvp_probability.csv")
players_df = players_df.merge(mvp_prob_df, on="Player", how="left", suffixes=("", "_ml"))

players_df['Model Rank'] = players_df['mvp_probability'].rank(ascending=False, method = 'min').astype('Int64')

display(HTML('<h3 style="text-align:center;">🤖 ML Model Rankings👇(scrollable)</h3>'))
show (players_df[[ 'Player', 'Model Rank', 'mvp_probability', 'mvp_score', 'Team', 'PTS', 'AST', 'TRB','BLK', 'STL', 'WS', 'team_win_pct']].sort_values('Model Rank').reset_index(drop=True), pageLength=10, lengthMenu = [10, 15, 20, 25, 50], paging = True, layout ={'topStart' : 'pageLength', 'topEnd':'search','bottomStart':'info','bottomEnd':'paging' }) #the reset_index line allows the table to look cleaner, it wont say the data stored number before the player anymore.

display(HTML('<h3 style="text-align:center;">🏆 Weighted Formula Rankings👇(scrollable)</h3>'))
show(players_df[['Player', 'MVP Rank', 'mvp_score', 'Age', 'Team', 'PTS', 'AST', 'TRB', 'BLK', 'STL', 'team_win_pct']].sort_values('MVP Rank'), pageLength=10, lengthMenu=[10,15,20,25,50], paging=True, layout={'topStart':'pageLength','topEnd':'search','bottomStart':'info','bottomEnd':'paging'})

```{python}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show MVP winner ages"
import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px
from pathlib import Path

csv_path = Path('mvp_live.csv') #this cell block will be to showcase, the average age of the MVPs.
df = pd.read_csv(csv_path)


grid= px.scatter(df, x="Season", y="Age", hover_name="Player", title="MVP Winners by Age", template="plotly_dark")
grid.update_layout(
    xaxis_title="AGE",
    yaxis_title="Season",
    title="Age correlation with the past MVP winners",
    showlegend=False
)
order = sorted(df['Season'].unique(),key=lambda s: int(s.split('-')[0])) #this is to sort the seasons in order, since they are strings and not numbers, it will sort them by the first number in the string


grid.update_xaxes(categoryorder='array',categoryarray=order)

import numpy as np
import plotly.graph_objects as go
# Add a trendline using numpy's polyfit
df_ordered = df.copy()
df_ordered['start_year'] = df_ordered['Season'].str.split('-').str[0].astype(int)
df_ordered =df_ordered.sort_values('start_year')

connect_line = go.Scatter( #this code allows us to connect the dots in the graph with a line.
  x=df_ordered['Season'],
  y=df_ordered['Age'],
  mode='lines',
  line=dict(color='cyan',width=2),
  showlegend=False
)
grid.add_trace(connect_line )
grid.show()
```

```{python}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show code"

import plotly.graph_objects as go

stats = ["PTS", "AST", "TRB", "STL", "BLK", "WS", "eFG%_norm", "team_win_pct"]
metrics = {"mvp_score": "Weighted Formula Score", "mvp_probability": "ML Model Probability"}

fig = go.Figure()
visible_index = 0
buttons = []
trace_index = 0

for stat in stats: 
    for metric_col, metric_label in metrics.items():
        fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
            x = players_df[stat], y = players_df[metric_col],
            mode='markers', text=players_df['Player'],
            name= f"{stat} vs {metric_label}",
            visible = (trace_index == 0)
        ))
        trace_index += 1
        
trace_index = 0 
for stat in stats: 
    for metric_col, metric_label in metrics.items():
        visibility = [i == trace_index for i in range(len(stats) * len(metrics))]
        buttons.append(dict(
            label = f"{stat} vs {metric_label}",
            method = "update",
            args = [{"visible": visibility}, {"title": f"{stat} vs {metric_label}", "xaxis.title.text": f"{stat}", "yaxis.title.text": f"{metric_label}"}]
        ))
        trace_index += 1
fig.update_layout(
    updatemenus=[dict(active=0, buttons=buttons, x=0.5, y=1.15)],
    #title=f"{stats[0]} vs {list(metrics.values())[0]}",
    xaxis_title=stats[0],
    yaxis_title=list(metrics.values())[0],
    template="plotly_dark"

)
fig.update_layout(margin=dict(t=100))
fig.show()
```
